summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe sclerodermatous graft-versus-host disease was admitted for fevers, cough, and worsening shortness of breath. He was found to have RSV pneumonia and bacterial pneumonia, leading to acute respiratory failure requiring intubation and ICU care. Treatment included palivizumab for RSV, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and diuresis for volume overload related to heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (30%). He developed transaminitis of uncertain etiology, prompting reduction of ruxolitinib and holding of several medications. His condition improved, and he was weaned off mechanical ventilation. He received IV immunoglobulin before discharge. He was discharged home on adjusted immunosuppressive, cardiac, and supportive therapies with plans for outpatient follow-up.
